newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Poll sees run-off in Czech Senate elections.
newsitem.headline: Poll sees run-off in Czech Senate elections.

text.p: A survey predicted on Monday a run-off between Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) and the leading opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) in Czech Senate elections later this month.

Independent pollsters Factum said that after an inconclusive first round 79 ODS candidates and 73 CSSD candidates were likely to fight in a second round for control of the upper chamber of parliament -- an advisory body with limited legislative powers.

The poll, conducted for the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes, Czech Radio and TV Premiera, asked 12,000 citizens from a cross-section of society in each constitunecy how they would vote in the first round scheduled for November 15 and 16.
The survey, the widest to date, showed there was likely to be a second-round run-off between candidates from Klaus's ODS and the opposition CSSD in 41 of all 81 constituencies.
Factum will release the results of a new survey asking voters who they will choose in the second round on November 22-23 on Thursday.

According to Czech law, if no candidate in a constituency wins over 50 percent of votes cast in the first round, there is a second round for the top two candidates from the first poll. -- Prague Newsroom 42-2-2423-0003
